issues.title: [Bug]: closed record with an optional `never` field is not a subtype of the same record without it
issues.output:
1520a: error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: incompatible type: expected {| a: int, never... |}, got {| a: int, b: never, never... |} (8:13)
1520b: false
true
issues.reasoning: Spec §5.4.2.2: an optional field only constrains the field if it is present, so `never b?` forbids `b`. R3 has the same shapes as R2, so R3 is a subtype of R2 (§5.1). A mutable value belongs to R2 iff its inherent type is a subtype (§5.3), so `v is R2` must be true. The bug is in the semtype subtype check. It shows up mainly as a front-end type-check rejection, and the same check gives the wrong runtime type test. The diagnostic also prints `b: never` without the `?`.

issues.title: [Bug]: list returned by `map:keys()` has no filler value (storing past the end panics "no filler value")
issues.output:
error: no filler value
        at main(1521.bal:6)
issues.reasoning: `map:keys()` returns a fresh `string[]`, which has no fixed length. FillMember (§7.15.1, §5.9.1) fills the gap with `""`. The list built by the langlib has no filler information.

issues.title: [Bug]: `array:fromBase64` / `array:fromBase16` reject whitespace allowed by Base64/Base16 literals
issues.output:
error("failed to decode base64 string")
[222,173,190,239]
error("failed to decode base16 string")
error("failed to decode base16 string")
issues.reasoning: The lang.array docs for fromBase64 and fromBase16 allow whitespace as permitted by Base64Literal/Base16Literal. That grammar allows WS (tab, LF, CR, space) between characters, so all four calls should return [222,173,190,239].

issues.title: [Bug]: type cast does not pass its contextually expected type to an inferred `<>` typedesc call
issues.output: error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: cannot infer typedesc argument for parameter 't': no contextually expected type (5:35)
issues.reasoning: §6.20: the operand of a type cast has as its contextually expected type the intersection of the outer expected type and the cast type (float|error). So `t` should be inferred as float. This is a type-checker gap. It is related to #1385 (the same symptom under `trap`) but is a separate code path.

issues.title: [Bug]: function with more than one `<>` inferred typedesc parameter is accepted
issues.reasoning: The spec on defaultable-param says `<>` "is allowed for at most one parameter in a function". A declaration with two must be a compile error, and it is not reported.

issues.title: [Bug]: unused-variable error hides the initializer's incompatible-type error
issues.output:
1525a: error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: unused variable 'x' (2:5) — no incompatible-type error
1525b: error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: unused variable 'y' (3:5) — no incompatible-type error
issues.reasoning: The initializer's static type must be a subtype of the declared type (§7.11), so an incompatible-type error must be reported whether or not the variable is used. Unused-variable errors are raised in stage 3 and stop the pipeline before stage 5 type-checks function bodies. Parent: #1155 (unused variables should be warnings and must not block compilation), whose fix would also fix this.

issues.title: [Bug]: XML template expression is rejected in a constant expression
issues.output:
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: expression is not a constant expression (3:16)
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: expression is not a constant expression (4:16)
issues.reasoning: §6.4 lists template-expr (and equality-expr) as const-expr. §6.6.2 says an xml template in a const-expr builds a read-only xml value. A valid program is rejected.

issues.title: [Bug]: including a recursive record drops the included field defaults
issues.reasoning: §5.4.2.2: included fields mean the same as if written out, and default closures are copied in. So Ext must get Tree's defaults `left` and `n`. Compilation succeeds, but the generated record-construction code leaves out the included defaults when the included record is recursive, and the resulting value violates its own type. Related: #1289.

issues.title: [Bug]: time:utcAddSeconds rounds sub-nanosecond fractions instead of preserving them
issues.reasoning: Utc is [int, decimal]. 0.9999999999 is exact in decimal, and adding 0 seconds should give [0,0.9999999999]. The native conversion to whole nanoseconds rounds it up into the next second. The package README lists this API as supported with no precision limitation, so this is valid: either keep decimal precision or document the limitation.

issues.title: [Bug]: time:utcAddSeconds wraps around at int max instead of panicking with NumberOverflow
issues.reasoning: Ballerina int arithmetic never wraps. Overflow is a panic. Normalising [maxint, 1.5] silently wraps to minint inside the native ballerina/time implementation, when it should raise an overflow panic or error.

issues.title: [Bug]: repeated xml:fromString gets progressively slower (new mapping type per element)
issues.reasoning: Every batch does the same work, yet the time per batch grows linearly. State builds up across calls: per the issue, NewXMLStringMap defines a new mapping semtype for each element. The spec sets no performance requirements, so this is a quality-of-implementation defect, not a conformance one, but it is still valid (unbounded slowdown and memory growth). `xml:fromString` is lang.xml, so it is categorised as langlib (values/xml.go).

undetermined.reasoning: Test-infrastructure flakiness, not a language or runtime bug, so none of langlib/triage-lib/frontend/backend applies. Did not reproduce locally: task-* corpus tests passed with -count=3 and again with -count=5 under 6 busy-loop CPU hogs on 4 cores, and TestSerialOpenCloseDuringCompilation passed with -count=10 under load. The code confirms the cause described in the issue: fixed runtime:sleep windows in corpus/lib/subset3/task-*.bal and hard-coded time.After(5*time.Second) in ls/core/compile/open_close_race_test.go:77,99. Looks valid as a test-reliability issue. Suggest a test/CI label.

Reproduced: `go test -race -tags debug ./projects/` reports 315 `WARNING: DATA RACE`. common.WithSuppressedDebug (common/debug_debug.go:56) mutates the global debugFlags while other goroutines read it in DebugWriteLazy. It is called from projects/document_context.go:86. Valid, but it is a debug-build tooling bug (release builds use a no-op), not a language-behaviour bug. The closest category is frontend (it happens during parsing). Suggest frontend or a tooling label.

Reproduced: the command at doc/guides/DEVELOPING.md:104 includes ./bir/... and ./semantics/..., where packages don't register -update (`go test ./bir/ -update` → `flag provided but not defined: -update`). It also omits ./nodebuilder and ./birgen, which register -update for the corpus/ast and corpus/bir goldens. Valid documentation bug, but no language category applies. Suggest a docs label.
